posts.text: Quebec does not allow NL to sell power through Quebec to other markets. (Meanwhile Alberta can build a pipeline through BC.) And higher power rates limit resource and industrial development in Labrador when it’s so much cheaper in Quebec.
posts.summary: Criticizes Quebec restrictions on Newfoundland power sales and market disadvantage
posts.quote: Quebec does not allow NL to sell power through Quebec to other markets. (Meanwhile Alberta can build a pipeline through BC.) And higher power rates limit resource and industrial development in Labrador when it’s so much cheaper in Quebec.

posts.text:
I don’t think many Canadians realize how much Quebec has benefited at NL’s expense.

Quebec gets 15% of its electricity from Churchill Falls and pays 0.2¢/kWh, denying NL significant revenue.

Quebecers pay 8.3¢/kWh for power. Newfoundlanders pay ~15.8¢/kWh.
